attribution_limitations: Two statements describe transfusion dependence: the case narrative says he became transfusion dependent (no time) and the discussion says about 3 months after therapy he became increasingly transfusion dependent requiring 1–2 units almost every 2 weeks. The source does not say they are the same event, so they are kept as separate facts and events; the cause was "not entirely clear".

The platelet count and smear sentence use "at this stage" after the five-day count sentence; the source does not state a separate date for them. Plasma cells "remain prominent" in the following sentence has no time of its own. They are kept in their own untimed event rather than the five-day event.

The marrow blast and promonocyte (2.5%/1%), plasma cell, light chain and FISH sentences that follow the 6-week and 18-week biopsy sentences state no time themselves; they are plausibly part of the same biopsy reports but the sentences do not say so. The paragraph-final marrow statement in the outcome paragraph (normocellular, trilineage hematopoiesis) likewise has no stated time. These results sit in their own untimed events, not in the dated 6-week and 18-week biopsy events; the 27% promonocyte/monocyte clause is part of the 6-week sentence and keeps that time.

Marrow blast percentages come from different measurements: more than 30% blasts (morphology), myeloblasts 14% plus monoblasts 23%, and a flow cytometry myeloblast population of 2% of total events; these are not the same measurement and are not reconciled.
The time from treatment to death and the interval over which he was effusion-symptom-free (6 months) are not tied to the biopsy timepoints; the date of hospice entry is not stated.
The phrase "normal MCV, and MCH" is punctuated oddly; it is read as both MCV and MCH being normal, since no other result is given for MCH.

The family declined "any continued supportive therapy (in the form of blood transfusion)", which suggests transfusions had been given, but the transfusion statement itself only says he was "requiring" 1–2 units almost every 2 weeks; the transfusion procedure is kept with action unknown.
